audience: NASA Space Apps Challenge judges and attendees: technically literate, short on time, not necessarily InSAR or landslide specialists.
communication_intent: Explain the problem and how the platform works first; then persuade the judges that PRECURSOR AI is a credible, reusable use of NASA radar data for the "Dancing with the SARs" challenge.
audience_outcome: Judges can say in one sentence what PRECURSOR AI does, which NASA datasets it uses and why it matters, and they scan the QR code to try the app.
core_message: Open NASA data in, one usable landslide early-warning map out: PRECURSOR AI sees landslides before they happen, from space.
delivery_context: Primary: presenter-led live pitch of a few minutes on a projected screen. Secondary: the deck is shared with judges as part of the submission and read without a presenter.
artifact_afterlife: Submission artifact for the challenge; reused as the base deck once the Lorem ipsum placeholders are replaced with real results.
content_divergence: Follow the supplied 9-slide plan: same slide order and titles, plan wording kept, Lorem ipsum placeholders kept as written. Steps 1-4 and Dashboard text on the How-it-works slide reuse the previous deck.
mode_behavior: Narrative arc over the user's fixed nine-slide order: the unseen warning sign (situation), data nobody can reach (tension), one platform and its pipeline (resolution), NASA data and impact (proof), phased roadmap, team and a scan-the-QR close. Slide titles stay the plan's labels as kickers; one short beat line per page advances the story. Lorem ipsum placeholders stay visible and are marked as to-fill.
image_notes: No photos or AI images. All visuals are native editable shapes: radar-fringe rings, a satellite pass over a slope, the six-step pipeline, the data table. The QR code on the last slide is a labelled native frame to be replaced with the real QR once the app URL exists.
